why.title: Why Circuit Diagrams?
why.body1: Circuit diagrams use standardized symbols to represent electrical components. This makes it easier to draw, understand, and communicate about electrical circuits across the world.
why.body2: Organizations like IEC (International Electrotechnical Commission), ANSI (American National Standards Institute), and IEEE create these standard symbols so people from different countries and industries can understand each other easily.

ui.selectInstruction: Select the correct circuit diagram from the options below

p1.question: Draw the correct circuit diagram for a simple circuit with one cell and one lamp
p1.explanation: The correct circuit uses a lamp symbol (circle with X), not an LED. Remember: incandescent lamps are represented by a circle with a cross inside, while LEDs have a triangle symbol.
p1.hint: Look carefully at the output component. Is it a lamp or an LED?

p2.question: Which circuit correctly shows a battery (two cells) connected to an LED?
p2.explanation: The correct circuit shows a battery (two cells in series) with alternating long and short lines. A battery requires at least two cells connected positive to negative. Option B only shows one cell.
p2.hint: Count the number of cells. A battery needs at least two cells!

p3.question: Identify the circuit where the lamp will NOT glow when connected
p3.explanation: In circuit A, the switch is in OFF position (open circuit) creating a gap. No current can flow, so the lamp will not glow. Circuit B has a closed switch allowing current to flow through the complete circuit.
p3.hint: Check if the switch creates a gap or completes the circuit path.

p4.question: Which terminal marking is correct for an electric cell symbol?
p4.explanation: In an electric cell symbol, the LONG line represents the POSITIVE (+) terminal and the SHORT line represents the NEGATIVE (−) terminal. This is a universal standard in circuit diagrams.
p4.hint: Remember: Long = Positive, Short = Negative. Think "Long Positive"!

p5.question: Which circuit correctly shows current direction in an LED circuit?
p5.explanation: Current flows from positive to negative. In an LED, the triangle points in the direction of current flow. The LED positive terminal must connect to the battery positive, and negative to negative for the LED to work.
p5.hint: Follow the arrow! Current flows from + to −, and the LED triangle shows the direction.

observe.title: Activity 3.1: Observe a Torchlight
observe.definition: A torchlight is a portable light source that uses electric cells (battery), a switch, wires, and a lamp or LED. When the switch is ON, the cells push electric current through the wires to the lamp/LED, making it glow so you can see in the dark.
observe.questionText: If we open the torchlight, what will we find inside?

cell.title: 🔋 Electric Cell
cell.content: An electric cell stores chemical energy and pushes electric charge from its positive (+) terminal to its negative (−) terminal when connected in a circuit. The metal cap is the positive terminal and the flat base is the negative terminal. When you connect wires from + to − through a lamp or LED, the cell supplies the energy that makes the lamp glow.

dc.title: Direct Current (DC)
dc.desc: Batteries provide DC electricity - current flows in one direction. Used in mobile phones, flashlights, and electric vehicles.

ac.title: Alternating Current (AC)
ac.desc: Wall sockets provide AC electricity - current changes direction. Used in homes for most appliances and lighting.

storage.title: Energy Storage
storage.desc: Batteries store electrical energy chemically, allowing portable devices to work without being plugged in.
